headline: Gold posts third consecutive weekly loss — $4,292 Friday low as FOMC week looms, positioning split signals floor
snippet: Gold fell to $4,292.11 on Friday September 12, posting a third straight weekly loss from the August high of $4,691. Silver held the $64–$66 range. Positioning data shows a split: institutional money remains net long while retail flows have turned defensive — a divergence that historically signals a floor ahead of a binary macro event. The September 15–16 FOMC rate decision is now the dominant near-term catalyst for the complex.

headline: GDX closes at $96.95 in textbook three-wave pullback toward $90 support — options call volume confirms upside bias before Fed
snippet: GDX traded a $95.30–$99.08 range on September 13, settling at $96.95 — a textbook three-wave pullback toward the 50/200-day moving average crossover zone near $90. GDX constituents are generating roughly $3,000 per ounce in operating profit at current gold prices. The ETF has surged 50% from its July low. Options market data shows elevated call volume, confirming institutional bias toward the upside into the FOMC decision.

headline: Five signals aligned before FOMC week: metals options flow, copper squeeze, HSBC $90 Brent call, COMEX reversal pattern — all pointing the same direction
snippet: Analysis published Thursday September 11 — when gold and silver sold off on hotter-than-expected PPI — identified five converging signals: (1) unusual options flow in metals ETFs; (2) commodity-index inflation warning; (3) copper margin squeeze from tariff whipsaw; (4) HSBC raising its Brent crude target to $90 on Hormuz disruption risk; (5) a COMEX reversal pattern on the daily chart. With the Fed meeting September 15–16, the setup into the decision is unusually symmetrical.

headline: Gold technical: $4,264 is the line — miners up 50% from July already lead every corrective leg and are expected to lead the next advance
snippet: Mid-September technical read: the $4,291–$4,264 zone is the make-or-break level for the current correction. Hold and the move is a textbook wave-2 correction before a third-wave advance; break and the next support is near $4,200. Gold bounced from that zone late last week. Notably, gold miners have led gold on both the corrective legs and the advance from July — a pattern that typically continues into the next primary leg.

headline: White House copper tariff plan stalls on affordability fears ahead of November midterms — Section 232 move frozen
snippet: The Commerce Department submitted its Section 232 copper tariff recommendation by the June 30 deadline, but the White House is hesitating over affordability optics ahead of the November midterms, according to sources familiar with the deliberations. Copper fell sharply on the news after briefly trading above $14,700 per tonne. A delay past the election would push any tariff implementation into 2027, removing a key near-term catalyst for North American copper producers and explorers.

headline: Copper whipsaws from $14,700 as tariff stall hits — Codelco H1 production down 11%, Northern Ontario juniors drilling through the volatility
snippet: Copper briefly broke above $14,700 per tonne before retreating sharply when the White House copper tariff freeze was reported. The price swing follows a broader pattern of tariff-driven whipsaws in 2026. Separately, Codelco reported H1 2026 production down 11% year-on-year, tightening the fundamental supply picture. Northern Ontario junior explorers continued drilling programs through the volatility, with several updated assay results reported.

headline: Kazatomprom's TQZ acid plant delayed 12 months by fossil discovery — uranium's largest miner exposed on sulfuric acid supply into 2028
snippet: Kazatomprom has pushed commissioning of its Taikonur (TQZ) sulfuric acid plant from Q1 2027 to a range of Q3 2027–Q1 2028 after a paleontological discovery in excavations triggered mandatory preservation protocols. Sulfuric acid is the critical reagent for in-situ recovery uranium mining. H1 2026 production was up 9% to 13,291 tU despite the constraint, and uranium spot remains near $90 per pound. The CEO described the situation as 'new realities' as nuclear demand shifts from policy discussions to operational execution, leaving reagent supply the binding constraint.

headline: Maritana bursts through 2 million ounces — 62% Burbanks resource jump builds WA gold hub case
snippet: ASX-listed Maritana (MRT) has updated the Burbanks gold resource in Western Australia to 13.7 million tonnes at 1.7 g/t for 755,000 ounces — a 62% increase adding 290,000 ounces from 6.1Mt at 2.4 g/t for 466,000 oz previously. Growth came from Burbanks North extensions. The company's total resource base now exceeds 2 million ounces across the Kalgoorlie district. Phase 2 drilling is underway and a further resource update is scheduled for Q1 2027. Proximity to the Black Swan processing hub is central to the project's economics.

headline: Faraday Copper closing BHP's San Manuel deal by September 30 — Arizona district targets 18-billion-pound copper future
snippet: Faraday Copper (TSX: FDY) is on track to close its acquisition of BHP's San Manuel copper cathode assets in Arizona by September 30. Under the definitive agreement signed July 2026, BHP receives roughly 32.5% equity plus offtake rights. Faraday shareholders approved the deal in August. Combined with the existing Copper Creek project, the district hosts more than 18 billion pounds of copper. Phase IV drilling at Copper Creek intercepted 100.8 metres at 0.22% Cu from surface, supporting the case for a future cathode operation.

headline: Rare earth September outlook: November 10 China export pause expiry is the key binary — germanium surges 10%, scandium falls 7%
snippet: The rare earth basket is near-flat month-to-date at +0.31% on average, masking sharp divergence: germanium is up 10.04% and scandium is down 7.36%. The November 10 expiry of China's export suspension remains the dominant binary event for the sector. Three scenarios are being priced: extension of the pause, selective reinstatement for allied nations, or full reimposition of controls. China controls 69% of mine production and approximately 90% of processing capacity globally, giving Beijing substantial leverage over pricing regardless of which scenario plays out.

headline: Lithium carbonate inventory surplus returns — ¥145,750 on September 9 as post-maintenance bounce fades, spodumene holds $2,137/t CIF
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate settled at ¥145,750 per tonne on September 9, down 1.15% on the day. The brief August spike to ¥149,000 — driven by maintenance shutdowns at China Minmetals, Tianhua Xinneng, and Jiuling Lithium — has faded as inventory builds resume. The price has recovered substantially from the ¥75,000 trough in 2025 but the supply-demand balance remains fragile. Spodumene concentrate is holding at US$2,137 per tonne CIF China, up 38% year-to-date, a better signal of upstream tightness.
